facts: Original and candidate parser loop conditions/back-edge are the same; candidate assembly emits .p2align 2,,3 immediately before the [datafile] whitespace-scan loop. The original loop begins naturally aligned without inserted padding.
Fresh current-order TU probe keeps 9 exact functions and the same historical predecessor for load_character_bmp; no peer code changed with the body overlay.

Three equivalent parser-loop exit formulations generated distinct complete COFF object hashes, but only two effective loader instruction/relocation identities: baseline, `while(ret){if(ok)break;}` and the negated equivalent compile to the same loader identity; `for(;;){if(!ret||ok)break;}` produces a second identity. All remain 1993-byte DIFFER.

A `-fno-align-loops` / `-fno-align-labels` diagnostic control does not change the complete object. `-fno-align-jumps` changes the loader to 1987 bytes and drops CU exact count from 9 to 2, so global alignment switches do not provide a useful recovery path.
ruled_out: Equivalent while/for exit spelling variants do not suppress the extra alignment contribution; two distinct spellings collapse to the exact same effective loader instruction/relocation identity.
The direct baseline overlay showed no upstream peer-code or emission-predecessor change, so current mismatch is not explained by whole-TU upstream context.
blocker: Local parser-loop exit spelling search has not found a historically supported source CFG that naturally places the loop head on the historical alignment boundary. Further local rewrites are low-information; next discriminating work is recovering the exact surrounding original branch/fallback source structure or using GCC pass evidence to identify which block placement sets this alignment, then replay that mechanism against similar blockers.
